frequency_question: How often do majority parties successfully pass their core partisan identity/electoral integrity bills when they make them a legislative priority within a congressional term?
membership_rule: Includes major legislation pushed by the congressional majority leadership targeting voting, election administration, or core partisan governance structures. Excludes routine appropriations, bipartisan compromises, and non-partisan technical fixes.

cases.name: H.R. 1 / S. 1 (For the People Act, Democratic majority attempt)
Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act (McCain-Feingold, bipartisan structural bill)
Help America Vote Act (HAVA, bipartisan electoral reform)
National Voter Registration Act (Motor Voter, Democratic majority)

provenance_note: claimed 2 hits but 3 of 4 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 4 named major structural/electoral legislative pushes; captures the friction of partisan will versus procedural and caucus limits.
known_gaps: Excludes minor state-level federal add-ons, focusing strictly on major federal voter eligibility or election administration legislative pushes.
skeleton: Major partisan electoral bills introduced by congressional majorities in polarized environments since the late 20th century.
multiplier: 4 observed attempts or major pushes in polarized eras resulting in 2 passes (mixed partisan/bipartisan), yielding a baseline conversion rate for high-stakes electoral bills.
validity_reason: Valid until the next major shift in congressional polarization dynamics and Senate rules structure following the 2028 elections.
